texts.li: The colony holds {COUNT} ideoligions now, and it shows. {A_nameDef} of {FAITH} and {B_nameDef} of {OTHERFAITH} both want the evenings, and neither will give way. {WHY}\n\nThey have asked the council to settle it.

{B_nameDef} says {FAITH} behaves as if the colony were already theirs. {A_nameDef} says {OTHERFAITH} has never once offered to share. {WHY}\n\nWith {COUNT} ideoligions under one roof, the council is asked how they should live together.

[b:faith:devout] {B_nameDef} eats standing up in the kitchen now, rather than sit at the table while {A_nameDef} says the words of {FAITH} over the food. {WHY}\n\nThe council is asked to find a way for {COUNT} ideoligions to share one colony.

[lowtech] There is one fire to gather at, and {COUNT} ideoligions that want it. {A_nameDef} speaks for {FAITH}, {B_nameDef} for {OTHERFAITH}. {WHY}\n\nThe council must say how the colony keeps its ideoligions.

li.label: Share the {ALTAR}: the ideoligions take turns
li.outcome: The ideoligions take turns at the {ALTAR} now: {FAITH} in the evenings, {OTHERFAITH} at first light, the others as they ask. The open-minded call it the fairest thing the council has done in a while. The devout are less sure.

outcomes.li: [b:faith:devout] {B_nameDef} keeps {OTHERFAITH}'s hour at the {ALTAR} to the minute now, and makes a point of leaving the place cleaner than {B_pronoun} found it.

li.label: A corner for each ideoligion
li.outcome: Each ideoligion has a corner of its own now, to keep as it likes. A few believers from different sides did the clearing out together, and argued only about where the broom should go.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] Each ideoligion has its own corner now, marked with a cloth or a carved post. The colony got on with clearing them out, side by side.

li.label: clearing a corner for each ideoligion
Name {FAITH} the colony's ideoligion
li.outcome: The council has named {FAITH} the colony's ideoligion. Its believers have taken to standing at the front. The rest have gone quiet, and the devout among them quieter still.

outcomes.li: [b:faith:devout] {FAITH} is the colony's ideoligion now. {B_nameDef} heard it out, said nothing, and went straight to {B_possessive} room.
[b:persona:curious] So {FAITH} is the colony's ideoligion. {B_nameDef} took it better than anyone expected, and asked {A_nameDef} where to begin.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has asked the council for an evening to speak for {FAITH}. Whoever wants to come may come, and nobody will be made to. {A_nameDef} says some of the colony have been asking questions.
[persona:warm] {A_nameDef} would like to hold an evening of {FAITH}, with the old stories, for anyone who cares to listen. It would mean a great deal to {A_objective}.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} asks for an evening by the fire to tell the stories of {FAITH}, the way they were told to {A_objective}.
[faith:alone] {A_nameDef} is the only one of {FAITH} in the colony, and would like one evening to tell the others what {A_pronoun} believes and why.

li.label: Hold the evening, and all are welcome
li.outcome: The council has given {A_nameDef} the evening. {A_nameDef} has gone off to find the right words.

li.label: An evening for those of {FAITH} only
li.outcome: The faithful of {FAITH} kept an evening of their own, and the rest of the colony left them to it.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} nodded and put away the notes {A_pronoun} had been making.
